title: Ghelion - A ship design game where you design/build ships, and explore a vast multiplayer galaxy - Made with Claude
author: Tr_uth_
selftext:
This is a concept I had been thinking up for a long time, that was inspired by a few other great games, about 3 months in. Those games that inspired me always lacked some key elements that always bugged me, namely that I wanted full absolute customization of space ship designs, and I wanted the ability to make huge ships / stations without my PC exploding. There is nothing like a group of players organizing to have a large scale space battle only for the game to crash. 

Ghelion is trying to solve this with some clever tricks (Which has pros and cons). Games like EVE Online have no ship customizations but they have huge battles that we love, then we got space engineers which is full custom but lags out easily do to the nature of block based games (As apposed to simpler 3d models like eve). The idea is to marry those two concepts together and have a game where you design the ship in a separate built in software I call the "Designer" (accessed from the home screen) 

The Designer is a block based building / design studio where you make the ship, upon completion it turns the ship into a 3d model that can be loaded into the main game. This solves the "huge ships" and "huge battles" problem because this 3d ship file can be shrunk down. Essentially you could have fully custom built motherships with hangers / fighters / rooms, and HOPFULLY if I did it right then you could have many of these in a system with little to no performance issues, all beating the snot out of each other.

The other half of this takes an idea I saw in another game which is a must, this is the microcontroller, where the game gives clever builders all the tools they need to make WHATEVER level of auto piloting code they desire. The microcontroller can talk to ship systems by running player made Lua code, and run these scripts to do... You tell me. Want to make a smart missile that launches and tracks other ships across the solar system, go for it. You want to actually do the math and steer the ship into a stable orbit around the sun, sure. Want to have a computer setup in the ship that plays flappy bird on it, its already been done and yes go for it. 

Still bugs here and there but feel free to give it a try. The idea of course is one large scale multiplayer world, on one 1000 star galaxy, containing 2590 worlds, wild west rules (none at all I mean).

[Ghelion.io](http://Ghelion.io)

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: Turning a finished ship into a smaller model sounds useful for rendering. I'm curious about the other part of a big battle: do Lua scripts keep running on ships far from the player? Twenty automated ships might still need a lot of simulation even if their models are simple. Have you stress tested that part yet?

replies.author: Tr_uth_
replies.body: The ship’s scripts run on the computer of the person piloting it, or whoever launched it if nobody is flying it. So they shouldn’t slow anybody else down: the server just shows everyone else watching your ship “the results” of what happened (your ship moves), the same as if a human was piloting it. On your end though, if you have 20 automated drone ships running off scripts you made, it would add some simulation, mostly the physics of flying 20 ships rather than the scripts themselves. I haven’t stress tested this specific scenario, but I’ve consulted with my wise partner Claude and we think a decent PC should handle it fine, while a basic laptop might feel it. The basic device should have no problem with a normal 1-3 ships running scripts.
